edges.description: HPGD encodes 15-PGDH, the main prostaglandin-degrading enzyme, so a pathogenic HPGD variant reduces prostaglandin catabolism. For p.Ser193Pro this step rests on the gene's function and on segregation, not on an enzyme assay of the allele.

Failure to degrade PGE2 raises its level. The rise is measured in HPGD-related PHO, where urinary PGE2 is high and its metabolite PGE-M is low. The isolated-clubbing report is MeSH-indexed for urinary PGE2 (Dinoprostone/urine), but its abstract gives no value and its full text was not available to this curation, so the size of the rise in isolated clubbing is not recorded here.

Raised PGE2 is proposed to drive the vascular and connective-tissue changes of the clubbed digit. The step is inferred from PHO and from clubbing biology, not shown directly in nail-bed tissue, and its intermediates are not established.
Expansion of the terminal pulp and thickening of the nail is what the clinical sign of finger clubbing consists of.
The same lesion in the terminal segments of the toes.

nodes.description: Persistently raised PGE2 is the biochemical state of HPGD deficiency. In PHO type 1 it accompanies clubbing, periostosis and pachydermia; in the isolated form only the digital component is expressed, which may reflect a smaller PGE2 excess from a hypomorphic allele. That dose explanation is a hypothesis. This node is not assumed for the SLCO2A1 isolated-clubbing family, whose serum and urinary PGE2 were normal.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase cause primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.
evidence.snippet: Homozygous individuals develop PHO secondary to chronically elevated prostaglandin E(2) levels.

nodes.description: Congenital clubbing of the fingers with thickened nails. It is the only clinical feature of the disorder and was present in all 11 affected members of the defining family.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in the HPGD gene encoding NAD+ dependent 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase underlies isolated congenital nail clubbing (ICNC).
evidence.snippet: we investigated a large Pakistani family with 11 affected individuals having hereditary congenital nail clubbing as a single invariable clinical feature without any associated ectodermal, skeletal or systemic imperfection

nodes.description: Congenital clubbing of the toes with thickened toenails. The disorder is defined as affecting fingers and toes, but the abstract of the defining report does not state toe involvement per family member, and isolated clubbing can spare some toes, so no frequency is given.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in the HPGD gene encoding NAD+ dependent 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase underlies isolated congenital nail clubbing (ICNC).
evidence.snippet: Isolated congenital nail clubbing (ICNC) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterised by enlargement of the terminal segments of fingers and toes with thickened nails

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous Missense Variant in the Solute Carrier Organic Anion Transporter 2A1 (SLCO2A1) Gene Underlies Isolated Nail Clubbing.
evidence.snippet: The thumbs are almost always involved, although some fingers or toes may be spared.

nodes.description: The tissue lesion of clubbing: connective tissue proliferates between the nail matrix and the distal phalanx, and the nail matrix functions abnormally, so the terminal pulp enlarges and the nail plate thickens and curves.

evidence.snippet: Digital clubbing is characterized by a focal bulbous enlargement of the terminal segments of the fingers and/or toes due to proliferation of connective tissue between nail matrix and the distal phalanx.

meta.association: Homozygous HPGD c.577T>C (p.Ser193Pro) in one large consanguineous family with 11 affected members (two-point LOD 2.98, multipoint LOD 3.62).

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in the HPGD gene encoding NAD+ dependent 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase underlies isolated congenital nail clubbing (ICNC).
evidence.snippet: A maximum two point LOD score of 2.98 ( theta= 0.00) was obtained at marker D4S2368 while a maximum multipoint LOD score of 3.62 was obtained with several markers along the disease interval.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion. Affected individuals are homozygous for HPGD c.577T>C (p.Ser193Pro) in exon 6, found by homozygosity mapping to 4q32.3-q34.1 and candidate-gene sequencing. The abstract reports no enzyme assay for this allele, so its functional class (complete or partial loss of function) is inferred here rather than demonstrated.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in the HPGD gene encoding NAD+ dependent 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase underlies isolated congenital nail clubbing (ICNC).
evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis of the candidate genes, in the ICNC linkage interval, revealed a homozygous missense mutation (c.577T>C; p.S193P) in exon 6 of the human HPGD gene encoding NAD(+) dependent 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase (15-PGDH).

nodes.description: 15-PGDH oxidizes the 15-hydroxyl group of PGE2 in the cytosol, the first step in PGE2 inactivation. Reduced 15-PGDH activity slows clearance of PGE2.

evidence.snippet: 15-PGDH is involved in the catabolism of prostaglandin E2 (PGE2).

nodes.description: Missense variant in exon 6 of HPGD, homozygous in all affected members of the defining family. The same homozygous variant was later reported in a five-generation Pakistani family with full PHO, so it does not predict the isolated presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation in the HPGD gene encoding NAD+ dependent 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase underlies isolated congenital nail clubbing (ICNC).
evidence.snippet: revealed a homozygous missense mutation (c.577T>C; p.S193P) in exon 6 of the human HPGD gene

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation in the HPGD gene causing primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy with digital clubbing in a Pakistani family.
evidence.snippet: revealed a novel homozygous missense mutation (c.577T˃C) of the human HPGD gene in all affected members of the family
